title: Streaming vs synchronous response-time facets by model & route
creator: Jordan Lee
description:
Goal: Build a consolidated dashboard and supporting telemetry to compare response-time percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and error rates across model + route combinations with an explicit streaming vs synchronous (streaming_flag) breakdown. This dashboard should make it trivial for SREs, runtime engineers, and PMs to: identify regressions introduced by model or kernel changes, verify streaming latency tradeoffs, correlate KV cache hit ratio and batching effects with tail latency, and drive routing policy changes when a model variant degrades.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: Hosted and Dedicated model routes; include model_version, route, deployment_mode (hosted/dedicated/private), tenant_id (anonymized), sequence_length_bucket, kernel_tag, streaming_flag. Show p50/p95/p99, request count, error rate, and KV cache hit ratio. Provide streaming vs sync side-by-side panels and a combined heatmap.
- Non-goals: Deep per-token breakdowns or instrumentation changes to model kernels themselves (that is separate instrumentation work).

Data sources and pipeline:
1) Traces: OpenTelemetry spans (ingested to tracing backend). We'll add a standardized span attribute 'redwood.streaming' = true|false and ensure trace_id is propagated from API layer through the runtime. Sampling: default 5% + full sampling for requests with latency > 1.5s during rollout window.
2) Metrics: Aggregated histograms exported from runtime to Prometheus/OTLP metrics collector; ensure we capture model_route.response_time_seconds histogram with exemplar linking to trace_id when available.
3) Logs: Structured request logs (JSON) in our logging pipeline include fields: model, route, model_version, streaming_flag, seq_len, kv_cache_hit, kernel_tag, tenant_tier, status_code, duration_ms. Logs backfill for 7 days, metrics for 30 days.
4) Join logic: Dashboards will use metrics for p50/p95/p99 where possible, augmented by trace-based percentiles for tail validation. Fall back to log-derived percentiles for routes without histogram exposure.

Acceptance criteria (must pass to mark Done):
- Dashboard UI: A per-model/per-route view with selectable filters for deployment_mode, tenant_tier, and sequence_length_bucket. Panels: (a) percentile lines p50/p95/p99 for streaming and sync overlay, (b) stacked bar of request volume by streaming_flag, (c) heatmap of p95 across model x route, (d) KV cache hit ratio correlated scatter showing tail latency vs cache hit rate.
- Data correctness: Metric/trace derived percentiles differ by <5% for p95 on routes with >1k requests/day.
- Instrumentation: 'redwood.streaming' tag present in traces and logs for 100% of new requests; exemplar trace_id attached to histogram buckets where supported.
- Alerting: Add p99 regression alert (relative + absolute) scoped by model and route to prevent unnoticed tail regressions.
- Dashboard docs: Confluence explainer with query examples, how to interpret differences between streaming and sync, and runbook for oncall.

Implementation plan (high-level):
- Week 1: Add streaming flag to API layer logs and OpenTelemetry spans; add exemplar exporting for Prometheus histograms. Create migration PR for trace sampling policy.
- Week 2: Extend metric names and labels in runtime (model_route.response_time_seconds histogram, kv_cache_hit_ratio gauge). Backfill short-term tests in staging.
- Week 3: Build Grafana dashboard panels + templated variables for model and route. Wire alert rules into Alertmanager and draft runbook.
- Week 4: Run dark launch on a subset of routes, validate percentiles vs traces, iterate on sampling. Roll out to all routes and handoff to SRE/Console owners.

Queries and examples (for Confluence & dashboard dev):
- PromQL example for p95 by streaming_flag: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(model_route_response_time_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, route, streaming_flag))
- Log-derived p95 example (pseudo): compute 95th percentile of 'duration_ms' grouped by model,route,streaming_flag using log pipeline's percentile() aggregator.
- Trace-linking note: when exemplar trace_id present, link panel will jump to trace explorer filtered by exemplar.trace_id.

Open links and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/streaming-vs-sync-latency-facets
- Staging PR (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3412
- Alert proposal: https://docs.google.com/document/d/alerting-streaming-vs-sync

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Tracing sampling too low to validate tail percentiles. Mitigation: temporarily increase sampling for flagged routes during validation, rely on log-derived percentiles as fallback.
- Risk: Metric label cardinality explosion (model_version + kernel_tag). Mitigation: enforce coarse bucketing (keep last 3 model_version tags, map kernel_tag to small set).
- Risk: Dashboard performance when querying high-cardinality combos. Mitigation: add pre-aggregated rollup tables for top-200 routes and use lazy loading for long-tail routes.

Handoff and docs: After rollout, schedule 1-hour walk-through with SRE and Console team, publish runbook and interpretation guide.
